description:
Landed 2026-08-11 by an agent that was STOPPED MID-TASK, so it never wrote tests or filed its own handoff. Found during the session-end sweep.

STATE. crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/zbs.rs is 317 lines implementing the Zehner-Bauer-Schlunder effective bed conductivity: new(), htr10(), deformation_factor(), radiation_ratio(), effective_conductivity(), stagnant_conductivity(). It contains NO todo!() and NO unimplemented!() — it is a real implementation, not a scaffold. It also contains ZERO #[test]. crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/mod.rs (41 lines) declares only `pub mod zbs;` so the tree is self-consistent and cargo check --workspace --all-targets passes with 0 errors.

THE PROBLEM. The whole acceptance criterion for this model was that it reproduce the verified 18-point reference table, and that check has never been run. An untested 317-line correlation is not evidence of anything — it is a plausible-looking implementation whose agreement with the reference is unknown.

THE ORACLE ALREADY EXISTS AND IS READ-ONLY. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/zbs.rs carries the 18-point Zehner-Bauer-Schlunder tabulation transcribed verbatim from the NRIC/INL Virtual Test Bed (reference-data/virtual_test_bed/htgr/generic-pbr/pbr.i), spanning 300-2000 K and 11.940293-44.9504677 W/(m*K), with an exact-at-nodes interpolant already verified (max relative error 0.0, monotonic over 1701 samples). Do not edit that file; consume it as the oracle.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Test the analytic model against all 18 points and record the ACTUAL agreement with a stated tolerance and date, per the V&V rule. If it disagrees, report the disagreement — do NOT tune the model to match, and do NOT loosen the tolerance.
2. Add the analytic limits, which are falsifiable and cheap: zero emissivity must recover the stagnant-gas-plus-solid limit with no radiation term; the effective conductivity must lie between the series and parallel bounds of its constituents; and it must increase monotonically with temperature once radiation is active.
3. State the homogenisation assumption in the doc comment explicitly rather than leaving it implicit.

NOTE the radiation contribution grows strongly with temperature and is what carries decay heat out during a loss of forced cooling. If it is wrong or absent the passive safety case looks better than it is, which is the specific way this model could quietly mislead.
title: tampines pebble_bed::zbs is 317 lines with ZERO tests — never checked against its reference table

description:
**Matrix solutions** on the hybrid backend. This is the highest-value item in
the epic — the linear solve dominates every FV timestep — and the hardest.

Existing serial code:

- `src/krylov/` — `bicgstab.rs`, `gmres.rs`, `preconditioner.rs`, `vecops.rs`
- `src/ldu_matrix/` — the OpenFOAM LDU sparse form
- `src/matrix/square_matrix.rs` — small dense

What to deliver, in rough dependency order:

1. **`vecops` on the backend** — axpy, dot, norm, scale. Cheap to port,
   immediately reusable, and a dot-product reduction is the honest first test
   of the GPU path. Note that a GPU tree reduction changes summation order, so
   results will differ from the serial path in the last bits; the parity gate
   must be a tolerance, and the tolerance must be stated.
2. **LDU sparse matrix-vector product** on the backend — the inner-loop cost of
   every Krylov iteration. Needs the host-side LDU-to-buffer serialisation
   (owner/neighbour addressing) done once per mesh, not per iteration.
3. **BiCGStab and GMRES drivers** that keep their control flow on the host and
   dispatch only the kernels. Do not try to move the whole Arnoldi loop into
   WGSL on the first pass.
4. **Preconditioners** — diagonal/Jacobi is trivially parallel and should come
   first. DIC/DILU are *sequential by construction*; they do not port directly,
   and the honest options are a block-Jacobi-over-subdomains variant (changes
   the preconditioner, so it changes the iteration count and must be
   re-validated) or keeping them CPU-only. Do not quietly substitute one for
   the other.
5. Dense `SquareMatrix` LU/back-substitution — small, so `CpuMulti` at most;
   flag it explicitly as not a GPU target unless batched over many small
   systems.

Known related work: `op-hzs.9` wants `outram-blender` to consume these sparse
solvers, and `op-ulo.5` notes the symmetric-solver (DIC-PCG / GAMG) seam is
still missing — so a CG path and GAMG are adjacent but out of scope here
unless they land first.

V&V: solve a system with a known analytic solution and a fixed-seed random SPD
system; compare CPU vs GPU residual histories, not just the final answer — a
diverging iteration count is the signal that a preconditioner was silently
changed. Record iteration counts and final residuals with the date.
title: outram-foam-basic-lib: matrix solutions on the hybrid backend (vecops, LDU SpMV, BiCGStab/GMRES, preconditioners)
